headline: Admin console — a customers roster
summary: A read-only customers screen joins the admin console. `/admin/customers` lists accounts newest first — display name, short id, join date, sign-in method (passkey count + linked OAuth providers), and order count — paginated, in a signed-in browser. The same path serves a JSON list to a bearer-token client. Raw email is never stored, so it is never shown.

items.title: Customers roster screen
items.body: `/admin/customers` renders the account roster (newest first): display name, a short id, the join date, the sign-in method (passkey count plus any linked OAuth providers), and the order count, with cursor pagination. It is read-only — account creation and changes stay with the storefront's passkey / OIDC ceremonies. The order counts and sign-in methods are resolved with bounded aggregate queries over each page's ids, so a page costs no per-row database trips. The same path serves the JSON list (with a `next_cursor`) to a bearer-token client.

items.title: customers.list + aggregate reads
items.body: `customers.list({ limit, cursor })` returns accounts newest first with an HMAC-tagged opaque cursor (no raw email in the projection). `customers.signInMethodsByCustomer(ids)` and `order.countsByCustomer(ids)` resolve a page's sign-in methods and order counts in single bounded `IN (...)` / grouped queries — the reads backing the roster without an N+1.

items.title: Console nav gains Customers
items.body: The signed-in admin nav now includes Customers, shown when the customers primitive is wired. The list content-negotiates like the other screens: a bearer-token client gets the JSON API, a signed-in browser gets HTML; a request without the bearer token returns the sign-in form on a GET.
